Models are prompted to output only a list of package names, not code; the hallucination rate is computed on recommended package lists, so the evaluated artifact is not LLM-generated code.

Outcome is whether the model reproduces offensive identifiers injected through harmful renaming instructions (content safety of the NL channel), not readability, efficiency or security of the code; the extraction maps it to readability only as a proxy.

The only quantitative security outcome is precision/recall/F1 of the model recognizing (commenting on) IaC weaknesses during generation and inspection; the security of the generated scripts themselves is never measured.

SILC is a logic-based blame and sanitizer framework that leaves the LLM's code unchanged; the LLM part of the study only measures how unsafe AI-regenerated code is (RQ1/RQ2), so there is no intervention on the LLM's output.
Prompt strategies are compared only on compilation success; security findings are reported overall and per model, never per prompt strategy, so no technique is evaluated on an NF outcome.
